To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the three coastal towns are all affected by the same range of issues around child sexual exploitation; (2) there is a need to understand and acknowledge the complexity of the issue and the different ways in which it is experienced; and (3) practitioners' perspectives on vulnerability and exploitation are not necessarily the same as young people's perspectives.
The three coastal towns are very similar to each other, in terms of the nature of the local economy, the nature of the CSE problem and the structure of the local response to it.

CSE is an issue that is not confined to any one geographical area, and that it is important to recognize the specific local factors which influence the nature and prevalence of CSE in any particular area.

the practices and experiences, rather than the effectiveness, of multiagency work.
how practitioners working in CSE partnerships make sense of their experiences and how they understand and interpret CSE.
the experiences of people working with children in three towns, and the ways that they understand and respond to CSE.
